key_insight: Referral wording largely reversed multimodal AI decisions between glioma and brain abscess on identical MRI images, outweighing imaging evidence.
clinical_relevance: These findings raise concerns about referral-text bias in AI-assisted brain tumor assessment; this study evaluated diagnosis, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Retrospective, single-center study of 60 MRI examinations: 30 gliomas and 30 abscesses.
Paired one axial slice per case with five referral texts and three prompt instructions across four multimodal models.
Collected 72,000 responses and descriptively compared performance with two blinded radiologists.
evidence_signal: Changing explicit inflammatory text to explicit tumor-suggestive text shifted tumor-call frequency by 79–100 percentage points; model accuracy was 52–73%, versus 78% and 73% for radiologists.
watch_item: Single-center, single-slice testing limits generalizability, and instructions to ignore referral text did not reliably eliminate its influence.
paper_title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess
